corinth_apollo.title: Temple of Apollo
corinth_apollo.text: Built about 540 BC and one of the oldest Doric temples in Greece: six by fifteen stocky columns, each shaft cut from a single block of limestone.

diolkos.title: Diolkos
diolkos.text: A paved trackway across the isthmus, several kilometres long, on which ships or their cargoes were hauled on wheeled cradles from the gulf to the Saronic sea, sparing the voyage round the Peloponnese.

acrocorinth_summit.title: Acrocorinth
acrocorinth_summit.text: The steep rock above the city, walled on its summit, with a small temple of Aphrodite at the top.

diolkos_hauler.title: Hauler
diolkos_hauler.text: Gangs dragged cradles with cargoes, and sometimes whole ships, over the paved diolkos.

strings.first_visit: Corinth, between two seas. Ships cross the isthmus on the diolkos.
strings.market_day: Market day: stalls, voices and goods from the country around.
strings.market_rain: Rain: the stallholders cover their goods and wait under the eaves.
strings.lamps_lit: Dusk: the lamps are lit along the street.
strings.wedding: A wedding: the bride is led to her new home with torches and songs.
strings.shearing: Shearing time: the flocks come in.
strings.threshing: The threshing floors are busy from dawn.
strings.vintage: The vintage: the grapes are trodden in the vats.
strings.rural_dionysia: The country Dionysia: a procession with songs, a goat and the aulos.
strings.season_turn.spring: The swallows are back under the eaves.
strings.season_turn.autumn: The grapes are in: the vintage begins.
strings.season_turn.nov: Cranes call high overhead, flying in a long V.
strings.season_turn.oct: The first rain. The whole land smells of dust and earth.
strings.season_turn.winter: The sea is closed. Ships are hauled up on the shore for the winter.

era.caption: Korinthos · {year}
era.note: still at peace: the war begins in the spring of 431, which the calendar never reaches, because spring returns to 432
